English writing studioA2 · 40-minute lesson
LET’S WRITE TOGETHER

Small ideas, bigger change.

Learn to write a problem–solution essay about making your town a cleaner place.

Start the lesson ↓Go to planningGo to writing
STEP 01 · 4 MIN

A cleaner place to live

TODAY’S GOAL

Write an essay that gives solutions to a problem.

Talk: What can you see in the picture? Where do you see litter? How does it make a place look?

Teacher: help with the words litter, bin and recycle.

STEP 02 · 5 MIN

Read a short model

Read the essay. Underline the problem, two solutions and their results.

What can we do about litter?

Litter is a problem in many towns. It makes streets and parks dirty. There are several ways to make our towns cleaner.

To begin with, towns could put more bins in public places. As a result, people would have a place to put their rubbish.

Another solution would be to organise clean-up days. People could work together to clean parks and streets. This would make the area cleaner.

To sum up, more bins and clean-up days could help reduce litter. Everyone can help keep their town clean.

Check together

Problem: litter makes places dirty. Solutions: more bins; clean-up days. Results: people have a place for rubbish; parks and streets become cleaner.

STEP 03 · 5 MIN

See the essay plan

Look back at the model. Which paragraph does each job?

1 · INTRODUCTION

State the problem.

Litter is a problem …

2 · SOLUTION 1

Give a solution and its result.

Put more bins …

3 · SOLUTION 2

Give another solution and its result.

Organise clean-up days …

4 · CONCLUSION

Summarise the solutions.

To sum up …

Keep the style neutral: avoid slang and contractions such as “don’t”.

STEP 04 · 5 MIN

Match solutions and results

Match 1–4 to A–D. Then say one full sentence using “This would …”.

SOLUTIONS

1. Put more bins in parks.

2. Organise clean-up days.

3. Set up recycling schemes.

4. Fine people who litter.

RESULTS

A. More rubbish could be reused.

B. People might drop less rubbish to avoid paying.

C. People would have somewhere to put rubbish.

D. People could clean streets together.

Check your matches

1–C · 2–D · 3–A · 4–B. Example: Towns could put more bins in parks. This would give people somewhere to put their rubbish.

STEP 05 · 5 MIN

Useful language

Use these phrases to connect your ideas. Complete the sentences aloud.

INTRODUCE A SOLUTION

To begin with, …

Another solution would be to …

People / towns could …

SHOW A RESULT

As a result, …

This would …

This could …

Towns could put more bins in parks. ________, people would have a place for their rubbish.
Check

As a result, people would have a place for their rubbish. Also possible: This would give people a place for their rubbish.

STEP 06 · 4 MIN

Plan your essay

Your task: write an essay about how to reduce litter in your town. Choose two solutions and note a result for each.

Problem: Litter makes …

Solution 1: …   →   Result: …

Solution 2: …   →   Result: …

Conclusion: Together, these ideas …

Teacher: ask “How will this help?” after each idea.

STEP 07 · 9 MIN

Write your first draft

Write about 80–110 words. Use your plan and the frames if you need them. Aim for four short paragraphs.

SENTENCE FRAMES

Litter is a problem because …

To begin with, … could …
As a result, …

Another solution would be to …
This would …

To sum up, … could help reduce litter.

0 words

STEP 08 · 3 MIN

Check and improve

Read your draft. Tick each box.

EXIT TICKET

Tell your teacher one solution and its result.

Improve one sentence in your draft before you finish.

If needed, finish the essay after class.
